name: Netflix
note: Works with libwidevinecdm0. Capped at SD-to-720p on Widevine L3.

name: Prime Video
note: Reliable on Linux Chromium. L3 resolution cap applies.

name: Disney+
note: Inconsistent on L3. Some titles refuse to start playback.

name: Max
note: Player is heavy. Expect slow catalog scrolling on the Pi.

name: Hulu
note: Blocks Linux browsers. Sends a Windows Chrome user_agent so the player loads.
user_agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/152.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

name: Paramount+
note: Generally loads on Linux. Live TV feeds are the flaky part.

name: Peacock
note: Loads on Linux. Heavy player, slow on first launch.

name: Apple TV
note: Web player prefers Safari. Playback on Linux is unreliable.

name: YouTube
note: Uses the TV interface, which is built for a d-pad. Best remote experience here.

name: Plex
note: Hidden: no Plex server. Set a url and remove "hidden" to restore.

name: Jellyfin
note: Local Jellyfin server. No DRM, so no resolution cap.

name: Tubi
note: Free and ad-supported. Light DRM, works well on Linux.

name: Pluto TV
note: Free live channels. One of the more forgiving players on the Pi.

name: Crunchyroll
note: Works on Linux. Subtitle rendering is CPU-light.

name: Twitch
note: No DRM. Full resolution available, limited only by CPU decode.

name: Spotify
note: Audio only, so no decode load. Good background option.
